etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: First attested in 1678: from Latin sēcrētus (“[having been] separated”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
paragraphs: First directly attested in 1728; attested as the past-participial adjective secreted in 1707: from Latin sēcrētus, perfect passive participle of sēcernō (“to separate”); reinforced by back-formation from secretion; compare secern; cognate with French sécréter and the Spanish secretar.
senses: (physiology, transitive, of organs, glands, etc.) To extract a substance from blood, sap, or similar to produce and emit waste for excretion or for the fulfilling of a physiological function.
